author: Md Jahidul Islam
title: 'Bangla Tesla' boom drains nearly Tk4,000 crore in power theft a year in Dhaka
key_facts: DMP identified 48,136 illegal charging points and 992 garages in 8 of 10 Dhaka crime divisions (2025); ~3,300 approved charging stations in Dhaka (2,100 DPDC, rest DESCO); TBS estimate ~Tk4,000 crore/yr transacted for unauthorised charging; EV charging tariff Tk10/unit vs >Tk14 top domestic slab; Dhaka distribution system loss ~5.5% (DESCO/DPDC officials)
theft_mechanisms: Tapping main lines and streetlight connections; dangling cables from poles; meters installed 'for compliance' while most charging is off-meter; commercial connections in residential areas without scrutiny; alleged accommodation by utility staff (owner claim); overnight charging
policy: Draft Electric Three-Wheeler Management Guidelines 2025; DESCO/DPDC raids and fines; city corporation crackdown plans
caveats: Rupee-value figure is a journalist estimate, not audited

author: TBS Report
title: Illegal autorickshaw charging causes Tk4,000cr annual revenue loss
key_facts: Home Minister in parliament (2026): ~Tk4,000 crore/yr revenue loss; >48,000 illegal charging points in Dhaka; 50-80 lakh battery autorickshaws nationwide; ~3,300 legal charging points; charging 'around 5% or more' of generation
theft_mechanisms: Illegal commercial use of residential connections; simultaneous charging overloads transformers and lines
policy: Planned registration, number plates/QR codes, driver licensing, digital tracking of vehicles and batteries; MP proposal for solar charging and zoning
caveats: Scope (Dhaka vs national) of Tk4,000 crore unclear

author: Shafiq R Bhuiyan
title: Can solar power help solve Bangladesh's auto-rickshaw electricity theft crisis?
key_facts: Cites unnamed study: ~500,000 rickshaws x 9.32 kWh/day; author estimates; Narayanganj ~50,000 autorickshaws (officials via newspaper)
theft_mechanisms: Unauthorised connections at informal garages; consumption not tracked by meters; transformer failures
policy: Proposes licensing charging, metered solar/solar-grid hubs, phased enforcement
caveats: Opinion; use only for policy options, not for numbers

author: Staff Correspondent
title: Battery-powered rickshaws create major traffic, energy challenges for government
key_facts: BPDB: 4.5-5 million battery rickshaws/easy-bikes; BPDB: post-midnight demand fails to fall by 1,000-1,500 MW, attributed mostly to charging; Power Minister: most charged after midnight via illegal connections, peak shifted to midnight; CPD: ~5% of generation (~750 MW)
theft_mechanisms: Post-midnight charging through illegal connections; staff attacked while disconnecting lines
policy: LGD drafting unified licensing; GPS/geo-fencing proposals; DSCC plan to shift to solar charging
caveats: 'BDT 4 billion' loss figure conflicts with Tk4,000 crore elsewhere (likely unit error); do not use it

author: SM Najmus Sakib
title: 'Bangla Teslas' take over the road despite policy gridlock
key_facts: Documents the nickname 'Bangla Tesla'; industry insiders: >4 million vehicles (2024); Power Cell director: ~1,000 MW daily use, accurate figures 'impossible to obtain'
theft_mechanisms: Mix of legal and illegal sources (officials)
policy: May 2024 Dhaka ban reversed after protests; 2021 draft legalisation policy pending; BRTA does not register them

author: Emran Hossain
title: Transmission loss keeps rising
key_facts: Power Cell: system loss 10.06% FY2023-24; distribution loss 7.25% FY24 vs 7.65% FY23; PGCB annual report: transmission loss 3.13% (2023-24), 3.07% (2022-23), 2.89% (2021-22); distribution loss 23.92% in 2002
theft_mechanisms: Households hooking onto live lines; CAB alleges theft with help of power-sector staff
caveats: Secondary report of official data: prefer BPDB/PGCB annual reports if obtainable

author: Staff Correspondent
title: Power sector losses persist, system loss rises, renewables progress stalls
key_facts: BPDB data: system loss 10.06% FY2023-24, 10.13% FY2024-25

author: Md. Khalid Mahmud; Khondaker Golam Moazzem
title: Integrating Electric Three-Wheelers into Urban Transport Network: Challenges and Way Forward
key_facts: ~6 million E3Ws nationally, ~2 million in Dhaka, ~5% registered in Dhaka; city table: 75-95% unregistered, mostly home/garage charging; E3Ws ~5% of generation (~750 MW) citing Daily Star 2024; 48,136 illegal vs 3,300 approved points citing Daily Star Dec 2025; garage economics (Kamrangirchar garage ~BDT 4,000 gross/day vs ~BDT 2,000 electricity); no E3W provisions in EV Charging Guidelines
theft_mechanisms: Drawing electricity directly from local lines instead of approved stations; informal home and garage charging
policy: Gaps: no legal definition of e-rickshaws; EV charging guidelines do not cover E3Ws; recommends LEV classification and type approval
caveats: Slides; many figures are secondary citations of newspapers

author: BSS; DPDC DGM (HR) quoted
title: DPDC installs 10.66 lakh smart prepaid meters to boost revenue collection
key_facts: DPDC: 10,66,005 smart prepaid meters installed of ~19,09,004 consumers (Oct 2025); prepaid introduced 2018; 5-7% non-technical loss at customer level attributed to meter tampering and illegal connections (statement)
policy: Prepaid rollout; 2% discount for prepaid users
caveats: Press statement; ministry claim that prepaid can cut NTL to zero is not evidence

author: BSS; BPDB Director (PR) quoted
title: PDB rolls out 33 lakh prepaid meters to boost revenue collection
key_facts: BPDB: 3,298,103 smart prepaid meters installed of ~42 lakh consumers (Oct 2025); three prepayment systems (Unified, STS, Smart); 5-7% customer-level non-technical loss (statement)

author: Shafiqul Alam (IEEFA)
title: Fixing Bangladesh's Power Sector
key_facts: T&D losses fell to 10.33% (June 2023) from 33.57% (1990, citing World Bank data); global average below 8% in 2022; recommends 8% target, saving ~2,222 GWh/yr and Tk24.44 billion/yr
caveats: Think-tank analysis; loss figure is T&D, not distribution-only

outlet: World Bank (Public Policy for the Private Sector, Viewpoint 169)
author: Lovei, L.; McKechnie, A.
title: The Costs of Corruption for the Poor: The Energy Sector (Public Policy for the Private Sector, Note No. 207)
key_facts: Bangladesh: revenue collected for only 55% of power generated; about half of BPDB and DESA system losses attributed by one estimate to mismanagement and petty corruption around metering; BPDB and DESA losses above US$100 million/yr; TI Bangladesh survey ranked utility staff among most corrupt officials; meter readers delegate reading to informal operators and run illegal-connection businesses; organised protection chain (unions, politicians)
theft_mechanisms: Meter-reading corruption; illegal connections arranged by staff
caveats: Historical (2000); qualitative evidence for collusion only

author: ADB Operations Evaluation Department
title: Special Evaluation Study of Cost Recovery in the Power Sector (SST: STU 2003-11)
key_facts: T&D losses in 2001: BPDB 24.9%, DESA 36.6%; countrywide total system losses above 40% in FY1991 and 37% in FY1994; rural electric cooperatives (PBSs) reduced losses to 13.9% with ~97% bill collection by end-2000; BPDB/DESA chronic non-payment
caveats: Historical baseline; different loss definition from current BPDB series

author: Power Cell
title: Year wise System Loss Statistics
key_facts: National distribution / transmission / T&D loss series 2001-02 to 2023-24 (2023-24: 7.25 / 3.13 / 10.06%); utility distribution losses FY2023-24: BPDB 7.23, REB 8.01, DPDC 6.04, DESCO 5.57, WZPDCO 7.38, NESCO 8.58%
caveats: Total loss only; no technical / non-technical split

author: Power Division
title: Electric Vehicle Charging Guideline
key_facts: Tariff set by BERC (sec 2.7, 6.12.1); only BRTA-authorised 2/3-wheelers covered (sec 5.1); separate meter for every public charging point (6.12.2); private station serving >3 EV owners counts as public (2.2); household tariff for private charging unless separately metered (4.1)
policy: Licensing via SREDA, safety certification, monitoring platform with penalties and disconnection
caveats: Does not reach unregistered battery three-wheelers

author: CPD
title: Recent Electricity Tariff Hike: Isn't there a better alternative for subsidy adjustment?
key_facts: Under the 2023 ministry mechanism tariffs were revised without BERC public hearings and without utilities disclosing their financial state (slide 11); BPDB comprehensive loss BDT 11,765 crore FY2022-23 (slide 15)

author: TBS Report
title: Business, living cost rise feared as BERC proposes Tk1.25 power tariff hike
key_facts: BERC technical evaluation committee: overall distribution losses projected at 7.37% in FY27 vs 7.38% in FY25
caveats: News report of a committee recommendation; final order not seen; whether 7.37% is an allowed loss in the revenue requirement is not stated
